properties.content:

Violation ID: 872571
Permit API: 129-26743
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: South Huntingdon Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-12-27
Comments: This inspection is being conducted as a routine inspection of wells in the general area. WQS Eric Norman is assisting. Conditions on site are cloudy in the mid 50's. The Access road appears to be constructed with no accelerated erosion or sedimentation observed. The site appears constructed and in production with one Production Tank on site. The Production Tank is within an earthen dike which appears to be in good condition. No dead, dying, or distressed vegetation is observed. The well is labeled and appears to be in good condition. The Production Tank appears to have corrosion forming on the bottom three feet of the tank. No holes observed during this inspection. The Department recommends that the operator take immediate action to prevent further corrosion from occurring in order to prevent breaches from occurring in the primary containment. It appears that an animal may have dug a hole under the Production Tank. The Department recommends that the operator abate this in order to prevent structural integrity issues from arising. The Department is requesting Production Tank inspection reports from 10/01/2019 to 12/30/2019 for this site. The Department is issuing violations based on observations made during this inspection. Additional violations may be forthcoming based on information provided in the NOV response.

Violation ID: 950897
Permit API: 129-25570
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Hempfield Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/06/2022
Comments: On April 6th, 2022, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a complaint received for the Schimizzi S&M1 Well Site in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. At time of inspection, the Act 9 sign and ERP were not present on site. Well appeared to be equipped for production. Well label with operator information is faded and needs updated, as recommended in IR 3262201. Earthen berm around production tank appeared to be stable and well vegetated. On the north side of the earthen berm, as reported by landowner, 6 pits have been dug by the landowner with the goal of planting evergreens. The production tanks did not appear to be structurally sound. Production tanks were visibly deteriorated with large holes around each tank (photo 2 & 3). Towards the bottom of the 1st production tank, there was a pin hole actively leaking production fluid to the ground (photo 7). There were several animal burrows around the base of both tanks. Conductivity readings were collected at several locations around the well site (photo 5 - 15). Collected readings as follows: East side of tank 2 (Or), south side of tank 1 (2.35 mS), west side of tank 1 (Or), north side of tank 1 (0.57 mS), west side of tank 2 (0.45 mS), Hole 6 (0.21 mS), Hole 5 (0.24 mS), Hole 4 (0.23 mS), Hole 3 (0.21 mS), Hole 2 (0.20 mS), Hole 1 (0.06 mS). Based on today's inspection and conductivity readings, additional violations are being issued. All violations cited in IR 3174464 and IR 3262201 will remain outstanding.

Violation ID: 8164642
Permit API: 129-24616
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Derry Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 11/02/2023
Comments: On November 2 2023, the Department conducted an inspection of the Keeno 2 OG Well in response to an OGI referral of the well head leaking fluid. Accompanying in today's inspection was Curtis Small (Pa DEP OGI).At the time of inspection, the well appeared to drilled. However, the well did not appear to be equipped for production. The production line from the well did not appear to be connected to a production unit or other visual production apparatus. The pump jack did not appear to be operational.The well tag was present on the well head. During the inspection, fluid was observed emanating from the well head in the location of the plunger rod. A background conductivity reading was taken and was 0.04 mS. Conductivity readings of the fluid were taken and they indicated elevated levels of contaminants with direct reading of the water of 0.30mS and soil readings of 0.15mS and 0.11mS. Elevated readings were detected in about a 2 foot radius around the well head. No distressed vegetation was observed and no waters of the Commonwealth appeared to have been affected by this release. Prior to leaving the location, the Department contacted Apollo Resources Representative Jame Stiffler to inform him of the release. I recommended that the Operator take immediate action to correct the condition creating the release and remediate the area in accordance with the Department's current spill policy. Mr. Stiffler indicated that they would sent someone out to correct the leak, and remediate the area as needed. Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the failure to properly control production fluid and/or other fluids resulting in a release to the ground. The Department requests clarification as to what caused the release, the quantity of fluid released and how this was determined, and how long it is believed the release was occurring. Please include the clarification information within the NOV response.

Comments: On August 25, 2025, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to the previous on-site inspection (IR 4031976), the Operator's update that excavation is complete (IR 4036853) and the NOV Response (IR 4036859).Act 9 sign is present. Emergency Response Plan (ERP) is on-site in the mailbox. Well head is tagged. No spills, leaks, or releases are observed at the well at this time. At time of inspection, no personnel from Diversified are present on site, however a crew is on site with earth moving machinery.A soil stockpile is observed along the access road just downslope of the site. The Department could not assess any further as a dump truck arrived on site and unloaded what appears to be new soil onto the stockpile. Unconventional: No

Inspection Date: 6/02/2022
Comments: On 6/2/22 at 0900 hrs., I conducted an inspection of Turm Oil, Inc.'s Paul Strong 4 well (API 063-34032) in Cherryhill Twp., Indiana Co. Mr. Bill Davis with Turm Oil was also present during the inspection. The inspection was conducted in response to a complaint, received by the Department on 6/1/22, of oil and produced water being released from a production fluids tank that was being removed from the site.I spoke with the complainant, the operator, and Mr. Davis on 6/1/22. The operator informed me that the well was sold to Rosebud Mining back in March; however there is no record of a well transfer filed with the Department. During our phone call, Mr. Davis informed me that the tank removal and release occurred around 1100 hrs. on 5/31/22. He estimated that approximately 10 gallons of crude oil and production fluid was released when removing the tank, and stated that some absorbent material was placed near the well and was subsequently containerized. Mr. Davis also acknowledged that some released fluid was covered up during regrading of the site.Upon inspection of the site, oil stained soil and vegetation was observed, beginning at the regraded area of the well pad, and continuing along a drainage ditch adjacent to the pad. There was a strong crude oil odor present. The impacted water in the ditch flowed to a nearby ephemeral stream where a slight sheen was observed. The black plastic bag containing the absorbent material Mr. Davis previously applied was located at the base of the well head; however, no additional measures were taken to prevent the material from reaching Waters of the Commonwealth. I advised Mr. Davis to place absorbent boom or pads to prevent further downstream impacts. I also advised Mr. Davis that regulations require removal of the pollutant from the soil and water within 15 days. In addition, I requested that Mr. Davis reinstall a well tag with the permit number on the well head.The release was not reported to the Department. Violations of 91.33(A), 78.66(a), 91.34(A), 78.66(b), and78.66(e) are cited and will be immediately closed as 'unresolvable'.Violations of CSL 301, CSL 307(a), CSL 402(b), 78.54, 78.57(a), SWMA 301, SWMA 302(a), and SWMA 610(1) are being cited for the release of crude oil and production fluid onto the ground and into Waters of the Commonwealth. These violations will be resolved upon remediation and temporary stabilization of the site, and submission of waste manifests for the disposal of impacted material to the Department.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/11/2022
Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 965084
Permit API: 053-27695
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Howe Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/11/2022
Comments: This conventional well is equipped with a pump jack, a site ID sign is posted on the location.Upon arriving on the location, I observed two areas of recent earth disturbance to the west/northwest of the well. The first area is in the proximity of a pipeline riser where patches of oil soaked soil remain across the excavated area. A second area located northwest of the riser (beyond the edge of the location) contains oil soaked ground and crude oil floating atop standing water in depressed areas. A third area of oil soaked ground/leaf litter was also observed approximately 100 feet into the woods to the west of the well. There are no signs of recent excavation in this area, there is no apparent surface connection between this area and the prior two.These observations indicate a recent partial cleanup of a crude oil release from the riser. Additional cleanup measures will be required throughout the area near the riser and northwest of the riser in order for those areas to be considered sufficiently remediated. As part of remediating the third area, due diligence should be given to establish the source of the product and any potential subsurface connection to the riser.

Comments: Arrived onsite as a follow up to a release of produced fluid reported on 7/7/25. The release was documented in inspection 4008591 from 7/7/25. I met onsite with Mike Deming and Creston Environmental.Two of the tanks had been removed and the containment adjusted. Some of the tanks and containment will need to remain in place while flowback continues. Flowback is expected to be completed by the end of July. The accessible portion of the pad was being scraped and free fluid was being vacuumed. Comments: On February 10, 2022, DEP representatives Brad Kline and Clark Smith conducted a follow up site inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Well Pad. The DEP met with STL Resources, and DEP showed STL Resources the area of high conductivity near the middle of the northwest infiltration berm that was found during an inspection on February 2, 2022. The DEP recommends exploring the area to verify if more excavation may be needed. The northwest infiltration berm area was screened with a soil conductivity meter and no new areas of high conductivity were found. STL Resources dug 8 test pits on the well pad to delineate the spill area and determine how deep the excavation will need to be to remove the contaminated pad surface. There was only one open test pit on the pad, the other pits had been backfilled. The conductivity of the side walls of the pit ranged from 400 uS/cm to 700 uS/cm. Soil sample 0651-098 was collected from the test pit. The contaminated soil pile remains on containment at the well pad. STL Resources is still awaiting sample results to be able to dispose of the soil to the landfill. The conductor rig was onsite in the process of drilling the second well cellar and conductor of four. No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227 and 3306834.

Comments: Routine field inspection performed in afternoon with cool, cloudy weather conditions, and 43 degrees. Last inspection performed on 6/5/16, more than 6 years ago. Wellhead is located in Agriculture field planted with corn that has been harvested ~750' NE of surface/ground production equipment (photo #1). The wellhead is not in close, visible proximity to the production facility. At the wellhead surface casing valve is closed, lower right side production tubular valve closed to port with valve cracked open to domestic house gas meter run, lower production tubular left side valve is closed, upper production tubular is plumbed with no valve unions, and the production tubular plumbed on left side (opposite meter) of head to sales/surface equipment with open valve; annulus is buried, unable to determine if vented (photos #2, #3, and #4). Meter reading with open supply valve (photos #4 and #5). A functioning pressure gauge in-line before drip/meter present, reading ~17 psi at time of inspection (photo #6). No Well label/marker is affixed to wellhead. The wellhead is not in close, visible proximity to the production facility and requires a well label/marker. Some trace to occasionally moderate corrosion at the wellhead on the production/surface casing steel unions, lubricator, and tubulars. Oil staining present on ground on the right side of wellhead. An unlabeled 55 gallon drum present at wellhead, but not plumbed or connected to any tubulars visible at wellhead with the word kerosene hand written on drum (photo #7). Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Well labeling OGA3211(H). The Department is requesting Operator affix permanent well label/marker at wellhead with well details present. The surface/ground production facility, one 50 bbl poly tank, and one 100 bbl steel tank all contained by a shallow earthen dike (photo #8). Valve open on main tubular feeding separator and open valves to and from separator (photo #9). A 31-day production chart is present with recordings and dated 5/2/22 (photo #10). Well posting signage affixed to steel tank with all information about well and current Operator present, except the Operator contact address information (photo #11). Oil staining present along ground and base of steel tank, with in containment (photo #12). Fair to occasionally moderate corrosion on ground production unit equipment and tank. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Well posting OGA3211(G). The Department is requesting Operator add contact address information to the permanent well posting signage affixed at the surface production facility. The Operator has not submitted 2021 Mechanical Integrity Assessment (MIA) for this well. No MIA submitted by the Operator for 2021, 2020, or 2019. The last MIA value officially submitted was back in 2018 stating 0 psig. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Operating Wells - Mechanical Integrity reporting 78.88(e). The Operator submitted annual production reported (APR) in 2021 of 0 Mcf recorded over 365 days. The 2021 annual production report submitted indicates that this well was not in production during the 2021 production year. Additionally, this well was noted as having 0 or blank production values under the gas and/or oil quantity columns and noted as Well Temporarily Not Producing under the non production comments columns of the 2019, 2018, and 2017 production reports. The last reported production value was in 2015 of 162.78 Mcf recorded over 336 days. Wellhead field verified and GPS coordinates of well updated with this inspection showed a minimal distance offset of ~17 ft between coordinates (photo #13). This well appears to be back in production based on this inspection, the chart at facility with recordings, and the open valves with meter at wellhead. This is an active, producing well with a domestic house gas meter at wellhead.

Furmanek reported that no additional soil movement has occurred since the slough was discovered. Repairs are reportedly expected to begin once the ground dries adequately to allow for machine operation. The access road and well pad appear to be stable at the time of inspection with no observable concerns relating to accelerated erosion and sedimentation (photos 2 and 7). Post-Construction Stormwater Management Best Management Practices (PCSM BMP) appear to be constructed in the locations shown on the approved ESP plan drawings (photos 15-21). The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (photo 1). The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan, Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) inspection log, and ESP approval letter are on site (photos 2-5). The ERP and PPC plan appear to contain the sections required by 78a.55. Seven gas wells are on site that appear to be equipped for production (photo 12). Well 6H is equipped with a well tag with no observable evidence of a fluid leak to the ground around it (photos 24 and 25). The well and operator's information are displayed and visible on this well tag, as required by OGA 3211(g) and OGA 3211(h).The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (photo 12). Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a Follow-up inspection of Seneca's DCNR TR 007 PAD D site in Delmar Township, Tioga County on 3/1/2023 at 1300 hours. Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/31/2026
Comments: On 8/31/2026, the Department conducted a surface inspection of the Orr 14 OG well in Washington Township, Fayette County. This inspection follows-up to IR 4266621, where violations were issued for failure implement adequate Erosion and Sedimentation control measures prior to conducting earth disturbances on the access road, which is resulting in a threat to the Waters of the Commonwealth. Diversified representative Jared Walker was present on site during this inspection.At the time of inspection, the following was observed:- The access road appears to be a multi-use road that is shared with additional Diversified well sites. Some tire rutting was observed in the shared access road. No Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) is installed at the access road entrance. Step 1.3 of the E and S/Restoration plan construction sequence is to install a Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) at the access road entrance prior to conducting earth disturbances.- The well site is located within a forested agricultural area. Compost Filter Sock (CFS) is installed downslope of the well site. Portions of the compost filter sock are holding minor amounts of sediment. In other portions of the CFS, the stakes appear to be dislodged. This does not appear to be affecting the functionality of the CFS at the time of inspection. However, the Department recommends that the Operator conduct maintenance on the CFS. Violations may be forthcoming pending re-evaluation of this location in a future inspection. Rig mats are being installed on the saturated ground around the gas well. The E and S/Restoration plan and a Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) are located at the Navaho Hollow Road entrance, which will not be used for well plugging operations. The E and S/Restoration plan is not specific to the Connellsville Street access road, which is being used for plugging operations. - The gas well is equipped with a well tag. A plugging rig and well plugging equipment have been staged on site. The Operator's information required by OGA 3211(G) was installed on site during this inspection by Mr. Walker (Photo 24).- Upon exiting the site toward Connellsville Street, the Department observed loose soil remaining adjacent to an apparent unnamed tributary to Downers Run (Photo 2). Although no sediment was observed entering this apparent unnamed tributary to Downers Run at the time of inspection, it is actively under threat by this site since no E and S control measures are installed in this location. Mr. Walker stated during this inspection that an E and S/Restoration plan specific to the Connellsville Street access road is drafted, but needs to be printed and installed on site. Mr. Walker also stated that correction of the ongoing threat to the Waters of the Commonwealth (WOTC), and installation of a Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) and additional CFS will be conducted on the day following this inspection.The Department continues to recommend that the operator take immediate action to cease ongoing threats to the Waters of the Commonwealth.Based on today's inspection, the violations for failure implement adequate Erosion and Sedimentation control measures will remain outstanding, as the threat to the Waters of the Commonwealth remains and tire rutting is occurring on site. Additional violations are being issued for failure to follow the E and S/Restoration plan and for failure to have an updated copy of the E and S/Restoration plan available on site.The violation issued in IR 4265922 for failure to post the Operator's information required by OGA 3211(G) on site will be closed in IR 4269231.

Unconventional: No

Comments: Evidence of stressed and dead vegetation in the vicinity of the Akins lease tank battery was visible from Rounds Hill Road. Brian Ayers (WQSS-DEP) and I (Mat Haemer WQS-DEP) were present for this inspection. This inspection was conducted to document findings of an apparent release of production fluids from the Akins tank battery, as well as a separate release from a brine tank previously removed from the nearby Loomis lease's tank battery. Kyle Miller of Trinity Mineral Partners previously indicated that he had checked and found the integrity of the Loomis lease brine tank to be sufficient for future use. Kyle indicated that the tank was empty and would be unused until repurposed.The PVC drain line within the secondary containment area of the Akins tank battery was found to be improperly placed. The PVC line straddles the cutout hole in the surface of the brine tank in such a manner that fluids draining through the line would be able to flow over the surface of the brine tank and pool within the secondary containment area. Soil within secondary containment immediately below the PVC line was found to have specific conductance in excess of 17,000 micro Siemens per centimeter. Evidence of pooling was visible in the containment area via crude oil staining and stressed vegetation. This indicates that fluid once filled the secondary containment, but apparently was able to migrate downward and/or outward through the secondary containment diking. Stressed and dead vegetation downslope and immediately outside the secondary containment dike further indicates the likelihood that the integrity of the secondary containment is inadequate. Understory vegetation was killed in an area approximately 30 feet wide by 200 feet long. Soils in the killzone were found to have elevated specific conductivity in excess of 2,000 micro Siemens per centimeter.The brine tank staged on location was found to have evidence of stressed and dead vegetation beginning from a point immediately beneath the drain valve and continuing downslope beyond the tank in an area approximately 10 feet wide by 200 feet in length. Specific conductivity in soils below the drain valve measured in excess of 8,000 micro Siemens per centimeter. Soils in the killzone downslope of the brine tank were found to have elevated specific conductance in excess of 2,000 micro Siemens per centimeter.Because the volume of this release exceeds the 1 bbl threshold, the use of either the Act 2 or Alternative Remediation Process is required.It is requested that Trinity Mineral Partners provide the Department with brine disposal receipts for the Akins lease. The Akins Lease Akins 1 OG Well was found to have an illegible ID tag.

Comments: In an effort to prevent the spread of the COVID-19 virus, the Department has conducted this administrative inspection in response to information provided by Chief. Based on the analytical results for isotopic samples collected by Chief at the above-referenced well on 6/17/2019 and 11/15/2019, methane was detected as follows: 32.92 % Methane detected at the Intermediate (9 5/8¿) x Surface (13 3/8¿) casing annulus on 6/17/2019. 42.43 % Methane detected at the Intermediate (9 5/8¿) x Surface (13 3/8¿) casing annulus on 11/15/2019. 93.64 % Methane detected at the Production (5 ½¿) x Intermediate (9 5/8¿) casing annulus on 11/15/2019. The presence of methane at the Intermediate (9 5/8¿) x Surface (13 3/8¿) casing annulus is evidence of defective cement. Although the presence of methane was reported by the submittal of the associated isotopic data, defective cement was not corrected or a plan to correct the defect(s) was not submitted for the above-referenced well. As a result, a violation of 25 Pa. Code §78a.86 has been cited, which provides: ¿In a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing, the operator shall report the defect to the Department within 24 hours of discovery by the operator and shall correct the defect. A broken pressure gauge was on the wellhead during inspection (photo #1). Notice of Violation (NOV) issued for mechanical integrity 78.88(a). Operator has not submitted Annual Production Report (APR) for 2020. Operator submitted annual production report (APR) for 2019 stating 0 MCF with comment that well is temporarily not producing. The Operator has reported this well like this since 2009. This well has not produced reported quantities of hydrocarbons since 2001. No house gas meter is noted on 2019 APR or present on location. Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 999887
Permit API: 015-21707
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Franklin Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/28/2023
Comments: Incident Inspection of Chesapeake's "Sensinger" Marcellus well site.Eric Hottenstein (Chesapeake) called the DEP yesterday (June 27, 2023) to report an estimated 20 barrel release of production liquid to the pad surface.I spoke with Eric Hottenstein by phone during this inspection. He explained the following: on June 18, 2023 a vac truck was removing liquid from the production tank. Apparently when the truck left, the valve on the tank was not fully closed, and the camlock plug did not seal. Yesterday Chesapeake's Well Tender saw liquid dripping from the yellow takeout can attached to the production tank. They were immediately able to get the leak to stop. The detection system on the production tank indicates that 20 barrels of production liquid leaked out of the takeout can during the ~10 days it was leaking. Creston Environmental obtained electrical conductivity readings from soil around the tank which indicated contamination from the leak. Hottenstein also explained the Marcellus well at this site produces Naturally Occurring Radioactive Material (NORM). I used a Ludlum 2241-3 meter with a scintillator probe to detect radioactivity. Background reading was 10 uR/hr. Readings ~1" from the production tank were 50-70 uR/hr. Chesapeake contracted Waste Management to decontaminate the production tank. They plan to remove the tank after decon on Monday July 3, 2023. Excavation of contaminated pad material will commence after tank removal. The production liquid release apparently infiltrated into the pad material around/under the tank. Vegetation immediately surrounding the production tank appears stressed (brown) from the leak. I used a Hanna Groline soil probe to get electrical conductivity readings from pad material surrounding the tank. The meter maxed out at 4.0 mS/cm, indicating contamination from the production liquid.Violations for the production liquid release are cited to the 015-21707 drilling permit. Due to the quantity of the release, cleanup is referred to DEP's Environmental Brownfields Program.Vegetation and rock stabilize soil of the site to comply with 102.22 Permanent Stabilization. I did not see accelerated erosion or sedimentation.Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies.Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. Pooled water on the pad surface in 4 separate puddles has electrical conductivity of 0.21-1.3 mS/cm with an Oakton PCTS5.Air temp 67FJLP
